name: bollinger_price_action_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY and BANKNIFTY, when the index probes a 5-minute Bollinger Band extreme (±2σ around the 5-min mean) and a single 5-second bar forms a rejection pinbar — low wicking below the lower band then closing up, or high spiking above the upper band then closing down — it signals that resting institutional limit orders and market-maker delta-hedging have absorbed the directional momentum flow. At NIFTY's band extremes, VWAP-benchmarked algorithms see price 15-25 spot points offside and aggressively lift offers (at the lower band) or hit bids (at the upper band), creating the pinbar's rejection wick. In low-VIX regimes (VIX < 18) where NIFTY oscillates in a controlled range, institutions defend these band extremes rather than chase breakouts, triggering a 10-20 spot point mean reversion toward the 5-minute midband within 30-90 seconds.

indicators.name: bb_upper
indicators.purpose: 5-minute upper Bollinger Band. NOT 12x the original (12×20=240 bars=20 min). Chosen at 60 bars (5 min) because: the original holds 5-20 min and uses 20-min BB for context; we hold 30-90s, so we need a shorter context window. A 5-minute window provides enough bars (60) to produce a statistically valid 2σ band while remaining responsive to intraday volatility regime changes. Shorter (20-30 bars) produces erratic bands that fire constantly on normal tick noise.

indicators.name: bb_lower
indicators.purpose: 5-minute lower Bollinger Band. Same 60-bar rationale as bb_upper.

indicators.name: bb_mid
indicators.purpose: 5-minute midband — used as the mean-reversion target anchor for exit. The midband represents fair value over the past 5 minutes and is typically reachable in 30-90 seconds from a band extreme.

indicators.name: bullish_pinbar
indicators.formula: lower_wick > wick_ratio * body AND close >= open AND low <= bb_lower * (1 + buffer)
indicators.purpose: Single-bar rejection signal. On NIFTY 5-second bars, a large lower wick relative to body means sellers drove the index below the lower band but buyers overwhelmed and closed it up within 5 seconds. This is a fast-execution confirmation that demand absorbed the supply at the band extreme.

indicators.name: bearish_pinbar
indicators.formula: upper_wick > wick_ratio * body AND close <= open AND high >= bb_upper * (1 - buffer)
indicators.purpose: Single-bar rejection signal. Large upper wick means buyers drove NIFTY above the upper band but sellers overwhelmed within 5 seconds. Confirms institutional supply defense at the band extreme.

conditions: bar's low <= bb_lower * (1 + band_touch_pct)  [bar touched or slightly approached lower band]
bullish_pinbar == True  [lower wick > wick_ratio * body, close >= open]
vix < vix_max  [default 18.0 — low-volatility regime where mean reversion holds]
bar's high >= bb_upper * (1 - band_touch_pct)  [bar touched or slightly approached upper band]
bearish_pinbar == True  [upper wick > wick_ratio * body, close <= open]

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (≈8 NIFTY spot points at delta ~0.5). If NIFTY continues 8+ spot points beyond the band extreme after the pinbar rejection, the institutional defense has failed and breakout momentum has overwhelmed resting orders. Typical NIFTY 30-second range is 2-5 option pts; a 4pt stop catches genuine failures without being triggered by normal noise.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points (≈14 NIFTY spot points). The 5-minute midband is typically 15-25 spot points from the band extreme on NIFTY intraday; we target 14 spot pts (lower end) for a 1:1.75 R:R. At a 60% win rate (consistent with pinbar setups on liquid indices), profit factor ≈ 2.6.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 18.0 (tunable 14-24) — mean reversion works in orderly, low-volatility regimes; VIX > 18 signals trend/panic where bands are broken, not defended
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:20 IST — skip first 5 min noise and last 10 min illiquidity
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index volume is structural and always present
filters.trend_filter: none explicit — VIX filter implicitly removes extreme trending regimes
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution model, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — Bollinger setups widely known, but pinbar confirmation on 5s bars is not easily frontrun; edge lives in execution speed

adaptation_notes: Original trades top-50 FnO stocks on 1-min bars using BB(20) with pinbar confirmation, VIX < 18, and nifty_return_5 as trend filter. Key changes: (1) Universe → NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index (smoother, more liquid, institutional flow dominates); (2) BB lookback → 60 bars (5 min) instead of 12×20=240 bars (20 min); compressed because we hold 30-90s not 5-20 min, and 5-minute context is sufficient to identify band extremes at 5s resolution; (3) Dropped nifty_return_5 filter — redundant on the index itself, adds noise since index IS the nifty; (4) Pinbar remains the core confirmation but applied to 5s NIFTY bars — large wicks on a single 5s bar are more meaningful on a liquid index because market makers respond instantly; (5) Stop converted from 1×ATR(14) to 4 fixed option points calibrated to NIFTY's typical 30-second range; (6) Target converted from midband (too distant for 5s) to 7 fixed option points representing a partial move to midband.
weaknesses: Bollinger Band breakouts on NIFTY during RBI announcements / FOMC: bands compress before event and expand violently, generating false pinbars
At 5s resolution, many bars will have small bodies (near-doji); wick_ratio filter may fire too often if body threshold is not floored
Pinbar quality degrades in low-volume periods (first 5 min, post-lunch); time filter partially addresses this
Crowding: Bollinger setups are widely discussed; but 5-second pinbar precision makes this harder to frontrun than 1-min setups
